description_full: Information Services Group, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as an artificial intelligence (AI) centered technology research and advisory company in the Americas, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. It offers digital transformation services, including sourcing advisory and cloud and data analytics; managed governance and risk; network and software advisory; technology strategy and operations design; change management; and market intelligence. The company also provides ISG Digital, a client solution platform focused on developing technology, transformation, sourcing, and digital solutions; and ISG Enterprise, a client solution platform that helps clients manage change and optimize operations in such areas as information technology, finance, human resources, and training. In addition, it offers ISG Research, which provides market analyses, provider evaluations, and data-driven insights; ISG Network and Software Advisory portfolio; and ISG GovernX, ISG Inform, and ISG Tango software platforms, as well as ISG iFlex, a delivery model for deployment of resources. The company serves private sector clients operating in the manufacturing, banking and financial services, insurance, health sciences, energy and utilities, and consumer services industries; and public sector clients, including state and local governments, airport and transit authorities, and national and provincial government units. Information Services Group, Inc. was incorporated in 2006 and is based in Stamford, Connecticut.

financial_summary: Information Services Group, Inc is a micro-cap technology business with a $282M market cap on $245M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +2.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $25M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -9.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.4×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 28% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

growth: Revenue has compounded at -5.1% over 3 years, -0.4% over 5 years and 1.6% over 10 years, so the decline is deepening.

Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.04, a backlog worth 49% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 3%.

own: Insiders own 28.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 71%.
